resources.string: Used by every part of the app set to “Follow Default”. Addresses in your tailnet always go through Tailscale while it is on, whatever the route.

The app’s own requests use it too: update checks, skill downloads, voice, weather and images in chats. A provider’s model list, usage and sign-in follow that provider’s route. Mirror speed tests always connect directly, to measure this network itself.

Runs inside Minis, without a VPN profile: only Minis\'s own connections can reach your tailnet, and only while Minis is running. “Use Subnet Routes” lets addresses that other devices share (such as a home network) go through Tailscale.
Finish signing in in the browser. Minis comes back by itself.
Tailscale did not return a sign-in page. Check the connection and try again.
No browser could open the sign-in page. Copy the link and open it in a browser.
The sign-in did not finish in time. Open it again and complete the sign-in in the browser.

Exit Node DNS: the shell looks names up through the exit node too. Off: it asks this device’s own DNS server, which sees the names and your real network, but DNS that only works on this device (a VPN app’s, a company’s) keeps working. Tailnet names always resolve through Tailscale.\nBlock Shell Traffic If Unreachable: a shell connection that cannot go through Tailscale fails instead of going out directly from your real address.
Sign out and remove this device from Tailscale?
The device key is deleted. Turning Tailscale on again adds this device as a new machine.
HTTP, HTTPS or SOCKS5 proxies. Passwords are encrypted with the Android Keystore.
Could not read that file as a PEM/X.509 certificate.

For a provider whose HTTPS endpoint uses a self-signed or private CA. The certificate is stored only inside Minis and is added to Android\'s trust anchors for this app; normal certificate and hostname checks stay on. It takes effect on the next provider request — no restart is needed.

Shell: a change reaches open shells from their next command; a program already running keeps the settings it started with. Backup: WebDAV, S3, SFTP and FTP servers follow this route; SMB servers always connect directly. MCP: HTTP MCP servers and MCP sign-in follow it; stdio servers run on this device and are not affected.
Shell: TCP and UDP connections and DNS follow the route (shells opened before a change keep the old one until restarted). Ping and connections from your tailnet into the shell are not supported.
This device\'s WebView cannot use a proxy, so the browser connects directly.
These hosts connect directly. Separate entries with commas or new lines; “*.example.com” also matches subdomains. Local addresses always bypass the proxy.
Create an auth key in the Tailscale admin console under Settings > Keys. It is used once to add this device and is not stored.
How this provider\'s requests connect. Set up Tailscale and proxies in Settings > Network.
Turns Tailscale and every proxy route off at once, without a restart: all of Minis connects as if nothing here were set. Your settings are kept.
Every connection is direct. Turn them back on to use Tailscale and your proxies again.
Checks each step a connection takes and says where it fails. The result contains no passwords or keys.
Minis listens on 127.0.0.1 for its own connections. Other apps on this device can reach that port but cannot use it without a password that changes every time Minis starts.
Providers not listed here follow the Default Route, which is Direct unless you change it. A provider\'s route can also be set on its page in Settings > Providers.
%1$d connections in a row failed (%2$s). Tap to choose whether to keep using it.
Everything routed through this proxy connects directly instead. The proxy stays in the list; choose it as a route again to use it.
Nothing is routed through this proxy any more.
Turn Tailscale off above to connect directly again, or keep it on and Minis keeps trying.
